output.summary: The shift-fatigue and new-operator explanations are not established. New and experienced operators have the same reject rate (8.8% vs 9.1%), and the late-shift clustering reflects batch tagging, not machining time. The yield decline is real: the measurement system, program and inspection criteria are unchanged, and the customer's PPM rise corroborates it. Spindle wear (out-of-limit runout, rising vibration, twice-deferred service) and Corvane hardness spread are confounded in time, so neither is established as the main driver. The Line 6 comparison (serviced spindle, Corvane bar, 8-hour shifts) is the discriminating test. Service the overdue spindles and run the controlled bar trial now. Do not report a root cause to Halvard, cut inspection, or put the new operators on improvement plans.
